title: Coefficients and sites
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring
$\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, an integer $n\ge1$, and put
$A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. The *coefficient stages* are
$\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, with constructibility, finite Tor
amplitude, constructible intervals and Tate twists. The integral, rational and algebraically closed coefficient conventions are those of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. On schemes where $\ell$ is invertible, their finite Tor conventions are [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], and Tate twists have the domain and coefficient conventions of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. At a finite coefficient stage $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, for a
scheme $X$, $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ is the full subcategory of the derived category
of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on the small étale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] consisting of the
bounded complexes with constructible cohomology sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes],
$D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)\subseteq D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ consists of those objects $K$ of finite Tor
amplitude: there exist integers $u\leq v$ such that $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[u,v]$ in the sense of [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. At this finite stage, for integers $u\leq v$, $D_c^{[u,v]}(X,\Lambda)$ is the full subcategory of $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ of objects with $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for $i\notin[u,v]$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. The constant complex $\Lambda_X$ is the constant sheaf $\Lambda$
placed in degree $0$ [def-kun-constant-sheaf], the unit of $\otimes^L_\Lambda$ [def-kun-derived-tensor].
Morphisms are separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

proof.text: Put $R=\Lambda_X$, the constant ring sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{\acute et}}$, and let $R[0]$ be its complex in degree zero [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. For a complex $C$, the total tensor construction [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] has only one nonzero summand in each degree in $R[0]\otimes_R C$ and $C\otimes_R R[0]$. On every site object $U$, multiplication gives mutually inverse module maps $R(U)\otimes_{R(U)}C^i(U)\rightleftarrows C^i(U)$, $r\otimes c\mapsto rc$, $c\mapsto1\otimes c$; on the other side use $c\otimes r\mapsto rc$ and $c\mapsto c\otimes1$. The inverse identities are the balancing relations $r\otimes c=1\otimes rc$ and $c\otimes r=rc\otimes1$. These maps commute with restrictions and hence induce inverse sheaf maps by the sheaf-tensor construction [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The differential is $d_C$: in the left tensor the sign is $(-1)^0=1$, and in the right tensor the term involving $d_R$ vanishes. This gives natural chain isomorphisms $R[0]\otimes_R C\cong C$ and $C\otimes_R R[0]\cong C$.

source.place: finite-stage constant-complex unit clause; direct calculation using Stacks Tag 03EK (sites-modules-section-tensor-product) and Tag 012Z (homology-definition-associated-simple-complex)

proof.text: For an acyclic complex $F$, the second chain isomorphism of Step 1 identifies $F\otimes_R R[0]$ with $F$, which is acyclic. Thus $R[0]$ is K-flat by [def-pc-kflat-complex]. The first chain isomorphism also shows directly that $R[0]\otimes_R F$ is acyclic, as required by the first-factor convention of [def-kun-derived-tensor].

source.place: Tag 06YN (sites-cohomology-definition-K-flat), applied to the degree-zero ring complex

proof.text: Let $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{\acute et}},\Lambda)$ and choose a complex $C$ representing it, so $Q(C)\cong K$, with $Q$ the localization functor [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. To compute $R[0]\otimes_R^L K$ by [def-kun-derived-tensor], use the K-flat complex $R[0]$ itself in the first factor; Step 1 identifies its tensor with $C$. For $K\otimes_R^L R[0]$, apply [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] to the ringed site $(X_{\mathrm{\acute et}},R)$ to choose a quasi-isomorphism $P\to C$ with $P$ K-flat. The derived tensor definition computes this object as $Q(P\otimes_R R[0])$. Step 1 identifies it with $Q(P)$, and inverting $P\to C$ identifies $Q(P)$ with $Q(C)\cong K$. Both multiplication identifications are natural: for a chain map $f$, the equality $f(rc)=rf(c)$ gives their naturality squares in every degree. These equations remain true after localization; they remain true for inverses of quasi-isomorphisms by composing with those inverses, and for composites by composing the squares. Consequently they give natural left and right unit identifications for the derived tensor product. This proves the assertion that the defined constant complex is its unit.

source.place: Tag 06YS (sites-cohomology-lemma-K-flat-resolution) and Section 06YL (sites-cohomology-section-flat); the unit is the explicit degree-zero calculation of Step 1

proof_origin.place: finite-stage unit assertion, expanded by the elementary multiplication calculation and the existing Stacks 06YS resolution theorem

lean.note: The published coefficient vocabulary is the exact implementation of this setting. DerivedCategoryModule is D(X_et, Λ); boundedConstructibleFiniteTor is D^b_ctf(X, Λ), the conjunction of bounded constructibility and finite Tor amplitude. boundedConstructible and DerivedCategoryBoundedConstructible provide D^b_c(X, Λ), constructibleIn and DerivedCategoryConstructibleIn provide D_c^[u,v](X, Λ), and constantComplex is the degree-zero constant Λ_X tensor unit. The source docs identify all of these with blueprint sk-def-sf-setting. The coefficient-stage choices A_{E,n}, O_E, E and Qbar, Tate-twist conventions, and separated finite-type morphism convention are supplied by the recorded dependency nodes and their declarations; no second definitions are introduced.
